description: future_ai dataset. Every section is optional in an import: omitted keys keep their current value, objects merge, arrays replace. Text fields accept tokens: {anchor_year}, {anchor_year+N}, {end_year}, {anchor:<anchor id>}, {param:<slider id>}.

model.outlook_notice: ⚠ Beyond roughly {anchor_year+9}–{anchor_year+14}, this becomes illustrative scenario modeling rather than a forecast. All curves are decay/saturation-bounded — uncapped exponential extrapolation is itself a hallucination risk.

energy_2026.label: AI electricity demand (model anchor)
energy_2026.source: Simulator anchor; review against IEA Energy and AI

token_cost_usd_per_million.label: Actual blended USD cost per 1M tokens

train_flop_relative.label: Largest frontier training run, relative to {anchor_year}=1×

computeG.label: Initial growth ({anchor_year})
computeG.tip: How fast total AI computing power is growing today. Epoch AI measures this at ~3.3–3.4×/year.

computeFloor.label: Long-run floor rate
computeFloor.tip: Minimum annual growth rate the model decays toward once capital, energy, and fabrication limits bite.

computeDecay.label: Years to half-decay to floor
computeDecay.tip: Years required for current growth to fall halfway toward the floor. Shorter means constraints bite sooner.

capexComputeCoupling.label: Capex→compute coupling
capexComputeCoupling.tip: How much extra compute-stock growth each 100% of capex growth adds (e.g. 0.15 = capex growing at its {anchor_year} rate adds up to +15% to the compute growth rate). Set to 0 to make compute growth fully independent of the capex slider.

capex.label: {anchor_year}→{anchor_year+1} capex growth
capex.tip: Annual growth in hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending, anchored at roughly {anchor:capex_2026} in {anchor_year}.

capexDecay.label: Capex growth decay rate
capexDecay.tip: How quickly annual capex growth cools toward a mature-industry pace, shown as its half-life: the number of years for the growth-rate premium above baseline to fall by half.

capexCeiling.label: Capex ceiling by {end_year}
capexCeiling.tip: Maximum plausible annual AI infrastructure spend by {end_year}. Prevents runaway compounding.

doubling.label: Task-horizon doubling ({anchor_year})
doubling.tip: Months for AI to double the human-equivalent task duration it can reliably complete. METR historical trend: ~{anchor:metr_doubling}. Drives the horizon, benchmark, and supervision charts below.

doublingDrift.label: Doubling-time drift /decade
doublingDrift.tip: Negative accelerates progress; positive decelerates it. Zero keeps the doubling time constant.

tokenGrowth.label: Token demand growth
tokenGrowth.tip: Annual inference token-demand growth. Epoch AI reports roughly 10×/yr demand vs 3–4×/yr supply growth.

costEffMult.label: Cost decline vs efficiency
costEffMult.tip: How strongly $/token cost decline responds to the perf-per-watt efficiency slider (Energy & hardware limits group). 1.0 = cost falls exactly in step with hardware efficiency; higher values mean software/model efficiency adds extra cost decline on top.

eff.label: Perf-per-watt efficiency gain
eff.tip: Annual compute-per-watt improvement from chips, software, and algorithms. Also feeds the cost-per-token decline (scaled by the "Cost decline vs efficiency" slider in Token economics) and the inference-speed chart.

ceiling.label: AI electricity ceiling by {end_year}
ceiling.tip: Maximum plausible AI electricity draw by {end_year}, accounting for grid and siting constraints.

limitYear.label: Node-scaling limit year (display only)
limitYear.tip: Display-only reference marker: draws the red dashed line on the Compute-stock chart at this year. It is not wired into any calculation — it does not change compute, energy, or any other curve — it is only a visual annotation for when sub-1nm node scaling is expected to plateau. Stored in data as years after the anchor year.

trainG.label: Initial growth ({anchor_year})
trainG.tip: Annual growth in the compute used to train the single largest frontier model. Epoch AI measures the historical trend at roughly 5×/year since 2020.

trainFloor.label: Long-run floor rate
trainFloor.tip: Minimum annual training-compute growth once power, capital, and data limits bite.

trainDecay.label: Years to half-decay to floor
trainDecay.tip: Years for training-run compute growth to fall halfway toward the floor.

trainCeiling.label: Compute ceiling by {end_year}
trainCeiling.tip: Maximum plausible training-run compute growth by {end_year}, as an order of magnitude multiple of {anchor_year}. Keeps absolute FLOP values physically bounded instead of compounding without limit.

openLag.label: Open-weight lag ({anchor_year})
openLag.tip: Months by which the largest open-weight model trails the closed frontier in training compute. Epoch AI Brief put this at roughly {anchor:open_weight_lag} in early {anchor_year}. Applied via fractional log-space interpolation, so sub-year lags (like 4 months) are not lost to rounding.

openLagDrift.label: Lag drift /decade
openLagDrift.tip: Negative narrows the open-weight gap over time; positive widens it.

chipGrowth.label: Annual capacity growth
chipGrowth.tip: Annual growth in advanced-packaging (CoWoS-class) capacity for AI accelerators — the tightest near-term supply bottleneck.

chipCeiling.label: Capacity ceiling by {end_year}
chipCeiling.tip: Maximum plausible advanced-packaging capacity by {end_year}, thousand wafers/month.

investGrowth.label: {anchor_year}→{anchor_year+1} investment growth
investGrowth.tip: Annual growth in private capital invested into AI companies, distinct from committed hyperscaler infrastructure spend.

investDecay.label: Investment growth decay rate
investDecay.tip: How quickly annual private-investment growth cools toward a mature-industry pace, shown as its half-life: the number of years for the growth-rate premium above baseline to fall by half.

investCeiling.label: Investment ceiling by {end_year}
investCeiling.tip: Maximum plausible annual private AI investment by {end_year}.

regionUsShare.label: US share of capex ({anchor_year})
regionUsShare.tip: Share of hyperscaler AI capex attributed to the United States in {anchor_year}. A breakdown of the capex curve above, not an independent forecast.

regionUsDrift.label: US share drift /decade
regionUsDrift.tip: Percentage-point change in US capex share per decade. Negative means other regions gain share.

regionCnShare.label: China share of capex ({anchor_year})
regionCnShare.tip: Share of hyperscaler AI capex attributed to China in {anchor_year}.

regionCnDrift.label: China share drift /decade
regionCnDrift.tip: Percentage-point change in China capex share per decade.

regionEuShare.label: EU share of capex ({anchor_year})
regionEuShare.tip: Share of hyperscaler AI capex attributed to the EU in {anchor_year}.

regionEuDrift.label: EU share drift /decade
regionEuDrift.tip: Percentage-point change in EU capex share per decade.

waterWue.label: Water-usage effectiveness
waterWue.tip: Liters of water per kWh of data-center electricity. Industry figures typically range ~0.3–5 L/kWh depending on cooling method and climate.

waterEff.label: WUE improvement
waterEff.tip: Annual improvement in water-usage effectiveness from better cooling technology.

optimistic.label: Optimistic
optimistic.tip: Sets every slider to a fast-progress preset: quicker compute/training growth, faster cost declines, shorter capability doubling times, and higher ceilings across all charts. A bullish trajectory, not a guaranteed outcome.

baseline.label: Baseline
baseline.tip: Sets every slider to the simulator's default, middle-of-the-road preset — anchored to today's measured rates (e.g. ~{anchor:compute_growth}/yr compute growth, ~{anchor:metr_doubling} task-horizon doubling) decaying toward typical long-run limits. The best-guess starting point.

pessimistic.label: Pessimistic
pessimistic.tip: Sets every slider to a slow-progress preset: slower compute/training growth, slower cost declines, longer capability doubling times, and lower ceilings across all charts. A bearish trajectory, not a worst-case floor.

card-anchors.title: Live data anchors
card-anchors.tip: The real, current data points this simulator is calibrated against. Check these before trusting any projection. All values are curatable via Import or the refresh button.
card-anchors.sub: Sourced figures every default and slider range is built from.

card-compute.title: Compute stock
card-compute.tip: Projects total AI computing power over time, decaying toward a sustainable growth floor instead of continuing exponentially forever. The red dashed line is a display-only reference marker for your node-scaling limit year — it annotates the chart but does not itself alter the curve.

card-parallel.title: Parallel task capacity
card-parallel.tip: How many task instances could plausibly run at once, assuming cost per parallel instance stays roughly constant so capacity tracks total compute stock. A rough capacity proxy, not a scheduling or orchestration model.
card-parallel.sub: Concurrent task-instance capacity, relative to {anchor_year} = 1×, log scale.

card-energy.title: Electricity demand
card-energy.tip: Projects electricity demand from AI compute, bounded by grid, siting, and policy constraints. Anchor: ~{anchor:energy_2026} in {anchor_year}. IEA’s ~{anchor:data_center_electricity_2030} 2030 figure applies to all global data centers, not AI alone.
card-energy.sub: Electricity demand for AI compute, TWh/yr.

card-water.title: Data-center water usage
card-water.tip: Derived from the electricity chart above via a water-usage-effectiveness (WUE) ratio, which can improve over time with better cooling. Industry WUE figures typically range ~0.3–5 L/kWh depending on cooling method and climate.
card-water.sub: Water consumed for AI data-center cooling, billion liters/yr.

card-token.title: Tokens vs cost
card-token.tip: Compares token demand against declining unit cost. Absolute USD price uses an editable {anchor_year} blended reference price ({anchor:token_cost_2026}); it is an illustrative anchor, not a universal market price. 'Inference spend' is demand × unit cost as a relative index ({anchor_year}=1×) — it is not a dollar figure.
card-token.sub: Relative demand, unit cost, projected USD cost per 1M tokens, and a relative inference-spend index.

card-speed.title: Inference speed / efficiency
card-speed.tip: Derived as the inverse of the token cost-decline curve: as $/token falls, effective throughput per dollar rises. An efficiency proxy, not a measured tokens-per-second latency benchmark — actual wall-clock execution time also depends on runtime and hardware factors this simulator does not model.
card-speed.sub: Efficiency-driven throughput proxy, relative to {anchor_year} = 1×, log scale.

card-train.title: Frontier training-run compute
card-train.tip: Compute used to train the single largest frontier model — distinct from the total AI chip-stock compute above. Anchor: ~{anchor:train_flop_2026} in {anchor_year}, historically growing ~5×/year (Epoch AI Trends).
card-train.sub: Largest single training run, relative to {anchor_year} = 1×, log scale.

card-open.title: Open-weight vs. closed frontier
card-open.tip: Models open-weight training compute as the closed frontier curve above, delayed by a lag that can widen or narrow. Anchor: ~{anchor:open_weight_lag} lag in early {anchor_year} (Epoch AI Brief, Jun 2026). A simplified lag model, not an independent forecast.
card-open.sub: Your settings only: training compute, closed frontier vs. open-weight, relative to {anchor_year} = 1×, log scale.

card-chip.title: AI chip packaging capacity
card-chip.tip: Advanced-packaging (CoWoS-class) capacity — the tightest near-term bottleneck on shipping AI accelerators, distinct from raw wafer starts. Anchor: ~{anchor:chip_capacity_2026} by end of {anchor_year} (TrendForce / Morgan Stanley reporting).
card-chip.sub: Advanced-packaging capacity for AI accelerators, thousand wafers/month.

card-invest.title: Private AI investment
card-invest.tip: Private capital into AI companies — distinct from hyperscaler capex, which is committed infrastructure spend. Anchor: ~{anchor:private_investment_2026} in {anchor_year}, extrapolated from $344.7B in 2025 (Stanford HAI 2026 AI Index).
card-invest.sub: Global private investment into AI companies, $B/yr.

card-capex.title: Hyperscaler capex
card-capex.tip: Projects hyperscaler AI infrastructure spending, bounded by a plausible ceiling rather than compounding forever. Anchor: ~{anchor:capex_2026} in {anchor_year}, or an imported override.

card-capexregion.title: Capex by region
card-capexregion.tip: An illustrative split of the hyperscaler capex curve above by region. Shares and their drift are set by sliders, not independently forecast per region — this is a breakdown, not a separate model.
card-capexregion.sub: Your settings only: hyperscaler capex split by region, $B/yr.

card-horizon.title: Task-horizon capability
card-horizon.tip: METR-style task horizon: the human-expert time a task would require, not wall-clock execution time. It does not say an AI works continuously for that duration. Anchor: ~{anchor:task_horizon_2026} in {anchor_year}. The long-range curve is bounded to avoid physically meaningless exponential values.
card-horizon.sub: Human-equivalent task length AI can reliably complete, minutes, log scale.

card-benchmark.title: Benchmark saturation
card-benchmark.tip: Illustrative capability-benchmark score (0–100%), modeled on the rapid-saturation pattern of benchmarks such as SWE-bench. It is not a named benchmark.

card-supervision.title: Supervision burden
card-supervision.tip: Modeled as 100% minus benchmark saturation, with a floor since some human oversight, verification, or governance is assumed to persist. Tied directly to the benchmark curve above, not an independent human-factors study. Real-world approvals, physical experiments, and external feedback loops are paced by the outside world rather than AI capability, so they are intentionally left out of this simulator.
card-supervision.sub: Estimated share of output still needing human checking or correction, %.

card-hardware.title: Hardware & physical limits
card-hardware.tip: Key physical and manufacturing constraints that could bend the compute-growth curve, independent of demand or capital. Qualitative reference only.
card-hardware.sub: Physical and manufacturing constraints on compute growth.

card-milestones.title: Projected task-horizon milestones
card-milestones.tip: These are human-equivalent task lengths, not claims that an AI works in real time for the listed duration or compresses them into a fixed number of hours.
card-milestones.sub: Year each human-equivalent task-length milestone is projected to be crossed.

card-reference.title: Expert forecast dispersion
card-reference.tip: Named external forecasts for calibration. The wide spread is the finding; the simulator should not be mistaken for a consensus AGI-date predictor.
card-reference.sub: Named external AGI-timeline forecasts, for calibration.
